key_insight: A biologically informed dual-branch transformer disentangles intrinsic cell state from drug-induced regulatory shifts to predict transcriptional responses across nonlinear dose–time trajectories, enabling accurate generalization to unseen cellular contexts.
problem_solved: Predicting how cells' gene expression changes after drug treatment is confounded by baseline cell states and complex dose–time dynamics; this paper addresses the challenge of isolating true drug effects and generalizing predictions to new cell types and conditions.
method: Dual-branch transformer architecture: one branch encodes baseline cell state, the other models drug-induced regulatory shifts; branches are learned to disentangle and then fused for prediction.
Biologically informed inductive biases: integrates pathway/TF-level constraints and explicit dose–time modeling to capture nonlinear temporal and dosage effects.
Cross-branch fusion (e.g., cross-attention) and training strategies that promote generalization to unseen cellular contexts and robust prediction of transcriptional responses.
impact: Provides a modular, interpretable modeling strategy for drug perturbation prediction that improves transferability across cell types—useful for ML practitioners working on drug discovery, perturbation design, and biology-informed model development.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: dual-branch transformer with labeled cell-state and drug-shift branches and fusion module.
Disentanglement schematic: before/after illustration showing separation of baseline vs drug-induced expression changes.
Dose–time response plots: trajectories or heatmaps showing nonlinear expression changes across doses and times.
Benchmark bar/line chart: performance on seen vs unseen cell contexts compared to baseline models.
paper_title: Modelling drug-induced cellular perturbation responses with a biologically informed dual-branch transformer
paper_authors: Yue Guo, Hao Zhang, Haitao Hu, Jialu Wu, Ji Cao
